Discover the project's e2e suites -- <tenant>-devops/e2e/<component>/Dockerfile,
each declaring an `e2e` stage -- the way `erun build` discovers docker/ and
`erun deploy` discovers k8s/, and run each one as a docker build of that stage
against a real, already-deployed environment. The e2e stage re-runs every time
while the stages before it stay cached, and the build keeps no image.

Each suite receives build args derived from the live environment, never
declared by the suite: ERUN_E2E_VERSION (the deployed version),
ERUN_E2E_BASE_URL (the HTTPS URL of the exposed service named like the suite's
directory), and ERUN_E2E_URL_<SERVICE> for every exposed service. The
.erun/config.yaml e2e.secrets list is passed as --secret.

--base-url points the suites at an address you name instead and skips the
exposure and certificate checks. --version sets the version the suites
expect instead of the deployed one. Because a --base-url may serve a
different deployment than the current scope, it needs either --version or
an explicit --tenant/--environment naming the environment it serves (whose
deployed version is then resolved); with both --base-url and --version the
environment is not read at all.

With no --component every suite runs, in order, and the exit code is non-zero
if any failed. Refuses before any suite runs, naming the cause, when the
environment is not deployed, a suite's service is not exposed or its
certificate is not yet issued, or its URL resolves to a loopback address a
docker build cannot reach. Also refuses a suite whose playwright.config sets
ignoreHTTPSErrors or hardcodes baseURL. A project with no e2e/ suite is a
clean no-op.

erun e2e is a separate step with its own exit code: `erun build`, `erun deploy`
and releases never run it, and it is not a release or merge gate. A failure
names the suite, target URL, deployed version, and log so it can be filed as
a bug; erun e2e files nothing itself.

Usage:
  erun e2e [flags]

Examples:
  erun e2e --tenant team --environment dev
  erun e2e --tenant team --environment dev --component erun-console
  erun e2e --tenant team --environment dev --component erun-console --base-url https://console.example.com
  erun e2e --component erun-console --base-url https://console.example.com --version <VERSION>

Flags:
      --base-url string      Run the suites against this URL instead of the exposed service's, skipping the exposure and certificate checks; needs --version or an explicit --tenant/--environment
      --component string     Run only the named suite (a directory under e2e/); default runs every suite
      --dry-run              Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --environment string   Target a specific environment; requires --tenant
  -h, --help                 help for e2e
      --tenant string        Target a specific tenant (default: the current scope)
      --version string       Version the suites expect (ERUN_E2E_VERSION) instead of the environment's deployed version

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
